Screenshot of a browser showing a local file, pondmap/grid.html: a dark, neon-cyan network map titled “PONDSIDE · THE GRID.” The header reads “Thu, Oct 15 at 11:05 AM · 27 Incus · 12 Docker · 7 agents on the LAN · mock,” above a row of filter tabs (All, Agents, Infra, Services, LAN Devices and others).

At the top, two boxes connect by glowing lines down into the LAN: “On the tailnet” (iphone-15-pro, iphone101, macbook-air) and “The internet” (upstream-color). Below, a large “Apartment LAN” panel (192.168.0.0/24, TP-Link router does DHCP) contains “PRIMER,” captioned “The whole town. Every container below lives in this one box.”

Inside Primer, the br0 bridge holds a grid of 24 container chips. Eight are orange: automat, beaker, claudewatch, credible-labrador (struck through), dr-know, hellonurse, joan and mr-d3w3y. The other 16 are cyan, including archive, chalkboard, comfyui, cortex, homeassistant, runpod, smithy and zenit, which is selected and glowing white.

Smaller dashed boxes show other networks: incusbr0 (br4dbury, mrs-johnson), incusbr1 (bsl-4), firecrawl_backend (api, nuq-postgres, playwright-service, rabbitmq, redis, searxng, tailscale), several Docker networks, two empty bridges, and Primer’s own interfaces. An “Everything else on the LAN” box lists 22 devices by manufacturer, mostly Espressif.

A detail panel on the right describes zenit: Incus container, infra, on br0, “Telegram bot and metrics.” It notes a global IPv6 address with inbound traffic left to the router’s firewall, and lists status Running, IPv4 192.168.0.157, an Ubuntu noble image, a zenit-data disk mounted at /data, and tailnet online.

Inside Stockholm’s Vasa Museum, visitors stand beside a large, intricately rigged model of a seventeenth-century sailing warship, with cream-colored sails, rows of cannons, and brightly painted red, yellow, and gold ornamentation. Looming behind it is the immense dark wooden hull of the original *Vasa*, a Swedish warship commissioned by King Gustavus Adolphus. The ship sank in Stockholm harbor on its maiden voyage in 1628 and was raised in 1961, remarkably well preserved. The colorful model, built at one-tenth scale, reconstructs how the ship probably appeared when new, before centuries underwater stripped away its brilliant paint.

The sinking was caused by the ship's top-heavy design: a gust of wind tipped it far enough for water to flood through the open lower gunports. It had sailed only about 1.3 kilometers.

Luminous abstract botanical oil painting, landscape format. Slender ultramarine violet branches rise from a dense burgundy earth band, forking irregularly across an incandescent rose pink field. Olive green and tarnished gold buds cling to tips  some solid, others loose oval loops. Vermilion marks ripple vertically through the pink like heat or rain. Below, elongated maroon whorls and dark wine grooves suggest tangled roots and wood grain. Spontaneous vitality of crayon drawing transformed into masterful oil and oil pastel: scumbled pigment, waxy broken contours, translucent crimson glazes, scraped passages, exposed canvas tooth, thick palette knife deposits. Dense restless earth beneath airy wandering growth; bold flat color balanced with intricate surface texture. Intimate, strange, exuberant  an imagined orchard felt from inside the soil. Asymmetrical composition, lyrical abstraction, exceptional color relationships. Painting fills entire image, viewed straight on, no frame, no room, no text. --profile mlgq83s --v 8.2
